intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy-21 (LGMDR21) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the POGLUT1 gene (615618) on chromosome 3q13.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy-21 (LGMDR21) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the POGLUT1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Study of affected and unaffected relatives confirmed correct segregation of the disease with the homozygous or compound heterozygous state for the POGLUT1 variants.
checks.explanation: Recessive LGMD R21 with homozygous or compound heterozygous POGLUT1 variants.

checks.claim: The POGLUT1 gene is located on chromosome 3q13.
checks.evidence_quote: Significantly, POGLUT1 is located within the 3q13.13‐q21.2 region of homozygosity in the affected siblings
checks.explanation: The paper places POGLUT1 in the 3q13.13-q21.2 region, which matches the draft's 3q13.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy-21 (LGMDR21) is a progressive myopathy affecting mainly the proximal muscles of the limbs. Muscle biopsies show dystrophic changes, fewer satellite cells, and reduced glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan. The disorder is caused by loss of the protein O-glucosyltransferase POGLUT1, which glucosylates Notch receptors, and is associated with reduced Notch signaling in muscle.

checks.claim: LGMDR21 is a progressive myopathy affecting mainly the proximal muscles of the limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: the patients exhibited muscle weakness predominantly in the proximal lower limbs, with onset during the third decade. The disease course was progressive
checks.explanation: The paper describes progressive weakness mainly in the proximal limb muscles.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in LGMDR21 show dystrophic changes.
checks.evidence_quote: Muscle biopsies from all four affected siblings revealed histological features ranging from very mild myopathic changes to classic dystrophic pathology
checks.explanation: The biopsies showed dystrophic changes, although these ranged from very mild to classic.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in LGMDR21 show fewer satellite cells.
checks.evidence_quote: we found a decrease in PAX7 mRNA and fewer PAX7+ cells in the muscle of patients compared with controls
checks.explanation: Patient muscle had fewer PAX7+ satellite cells.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in LGMDR21 show reduced glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan.
checks.evidence_quote: Western blots showed a reduction in α‐dystroglycan glycosylation in patient muscle
checks.explanation: Patient muscle showed reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation.

checks.claim: LGMDR21 is caused by loss of the protein O-glucosyltransferase POGLUT1.
checks.evidence_quote: The D233E mutation dramatically reduces the O‐glucosyltransferase activity of POGLUT1
checks.explanation: The paper describes reduced enzyme activity, not loss. The mutant protein is expressed normally and keeps some activity.

checks.claim: POGLUT1 glucosylates Notch receptors.
checks.evidence_quote: POGLUT1 is the sole enzyme that directly adds O‐glucose to a distinct serine residue of epidermal growth factor‐like (EGF) repeats containing a CXSX(P/A)C consensus sequence (Rana et al, 2011), many of which are found in Notch extracellular domains
checks.explanation: The paper states that POGLUT1 adds O-glucose to EGF repeats found in Notch.

checks.claim: LGMDR21 is associated with reduced Notch signaling in muscle.
checks.evidence_quote: Muscles from patients revealed decreased Notch signaling, dramatic reduction in satellite cell pool
checks.explanation: Patient muscle showed reduced Notch signaling.

paragraphs.text: This disorder was first designated limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2Z (LGMD2Z). Under the revised LGMD nomenclature it is LGMDR21.

checks.claim: The disorder caused by POGLUT1 mutation was first designated limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2Z (LGMD2Z).
checks.evidence_quote: OMIM# 617232 named as LGMD2Z or LGMD R21 POGLUT1-related
checks.explanation: The paper gives both names but does not say LGMD2Z was the original designation.

checks.claim: Under the revised LGMD nomenclature, LGMD2Z is designated LGMDR21.
checks.evidence_quote: OMIM# 617232 named as LGMD2Z or LGMD R21 POGLUT1-related
checks.explanation: The paper equates LGMD2Z with LGMD R21.

paragraphs.text: Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) reported a consanguineous family with an autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy that began in adulthood. Affected members had progressive proximal muscle weakness. Muscle biopsies showed dystrophic features, reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation, and fewer satellite cells.

checks.claim: Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) reported a consanguineous family with an autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: A consanguineous family from southern Spain comprises 17 individuals spanning three generations (Fig 1A). Four out of five siblings from generation II presented a phenotype consistent with a limb‐girdle muscular dystrophy.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a consanguineous family with a recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.

checks.claim: The limb-girdle muscular dystrophy in the consanguineous family reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) began in adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: with onset during the third decade
checks.explanation: Onset in the third decade means the disease began in adulthood.

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous family reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) had progressive proximal muscle weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: the patients exhibited muscle weakness predominantly in the proximal lower limbs, with onset during the third decade. The disease course was progressive
checks.explanation: Affected members had progressive weakness of the proximal muscles.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies from affected members of the family reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) showed dystrophic features.
checks.evidence_quote: Muscle biopsies from all four affected siblings revealed histological features ranging from very mild myopathic changes to classic dystrophic pathology
checks.explanation: The biopsies showed dystrophic features.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies from affected members of the family reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) showed reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed a variable reduction in the glycosylated form of α‐dystroglycan at the sarcolemma in patients
checks.explanation: Patient muscle showed reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies from affected members of the family reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) showed fewer satellite cells.
checks.evidence_quote: we found a decrease in PAX7 mRNA and fewer PAX7+ cells in the muscle of patients compared with controls
checks.explanation: Patient muscle had fewer satellite cells.

paragraphs.text: Servian-Morilla et al. (2020) reported more patients with biallelic POGLUT1 mutations. These patients had a myopathy with variable age at onset, mainly affecting the limb-girdle muscles. Muscle MRI showed a distinctive pattern of involvement: inner (medial) parts of the thigh muscles were affected, while outer parts were relatively spared. Biopsies again showed fewer satellite cells and alpha-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation.

checks.claim: Servian-Morilla et al. (2020) reported additional patients with biallelic POGLUT1 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we describe 15 patients from nine unrelated families from different countries carrying novel biallelic mutations in POGLUT1
checks.explanation: Additional patients with biallelic mutations were reported.

checks.claim: The patients with biallelic POGLUT1 mutations reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2020) had a myopathy with variable age at onset.
checks.evidence_quote: The most relevant variability among the whole cohort was observed in the age at onset, ranging from the 1st to the 5th decade, identifying congenital, infantile and adult onset patients.
checks.explanation: Age at onset varied from congenital to adult.

checks.claim: The myopathy in the patients with biallelic POGLUT1 mutations reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2020) mainly affected the limb-girdle muscles.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients carrying novel mutations in POGLUT1 all displayed a clinical picture of limb-girdle muscle weakness.
checks.explanation: All patients had limb-girdle weakness.

checks.claim: Muscle MRI in the POGLUT1 patients reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2020) showed involvement of the inner (medial) parts of the thigh muscles with relative sparing of the outer parts.
checks.evidence_quote: The muscle imaging pattern resembled an "inside-to-outside" fatty degeneration because the most affected segment was the inner region of each muscle in the anterior and posterior compartment of the thigh.
checks.explanation: The paper means the inner (internal or central) region of each muscle, not the medial side. The parenthetical 'medial' misstates the pattern.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in the POGLUT1 patients reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2020) showed fewer satellite cells.
checks.evidence_quote: quantification of PAX7+ cells revealed that the number of SC in LGMD R21 patients (n = 5) showed a significant reduction compared to healthy controls (n = 5).
checks.explanation: Satellite cells were reduced in patient biopsies.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in the POGLUT1 patients reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2020) showed alpha-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation.
checks.evidence_quote: We analyzed muscle biopsies carrying seven out of nine novel mutations described in our cohort of patients, and all of them showed α-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation
checks.explanation: All analysed biopsies showed α-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of LGMDR21 in the family reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of LGMDR21 in the family reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: In a family with autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, we identified a missense mutation in POGLUT1
checks.explanation: The paper describes autosomal recessive inheritance in a consanguineous family carrying a homozygous mutation.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous family with LGMD, Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) found a homozygous missense mutation in the POGLUT1 gene, asp233-to-glu (D233E). In functional studies, the mutant enzyme had reduced O-glucosyltransferase activity on Notch. Patient muscle and cells showed reduced NOTCH1 signaling, fewer satellite cells, and abnormal myogenic differentiation. These findings suggested that impaired Notch signaling and loss of satellite cells contribute to the disease.

checks.claim: Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) studied affected members of a consanguineous family with LGMD.
checks.evidence_quote: A consanguineous family from southern Spain comprises 17 individuals spanning three generations
checks.explanation: The study was of a consanguineous family.

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous LGMD family reported by Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) carried a homozygous missense mutation in the POGLUT1 gene, asp233-to-glu (D233E).
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report a homozygous missense mutation (D233E) in the protein O‐glucosyltransferase 1 gene, POGLUT1, in four siblings with autosomal recessive limb‐girdle muscular dystrophy.
checks.explanation: The paper reports homozygous D233E in the affected siblings.

checks.claim: In functional studies by Servian-Morilla et al. (2016), the POGLUT1 D233E mutant enzyme had reduced O-glucosyltransferase activity on Notch.
checks.evidence_quote: POGLUT1D233E also showed lower activity than wild type toward five different single EGF repeats from mouse Notch1
checks.explanation: The mutant enzyme had reduced activity on Notch EGF repeats.

checks.claim: Muscle and cells from patients with the homozygous POGLUT1 D233E mutation showed reduced NOTCH1 signaling.
checks.evidence_quote: Decreases in Notch1‐intracellular domain expression and in HES1 mRNA levels in skeletal muscle were detected compared with controls
checks.explanation: Reduced Notch1 signaling was measured directly only in patient muscle. In patient cells it was inferred from their behavior, which NICD overexpression rescued.

checks.claim: Muscle from patients with the homozygous POGLUT1 D233E mutation showed fewer satellite cells.
checks.evidence_quote: we found a decrease in PAX7 mRNA and fewer PAX7+ cells in the muscle of patients compared with controls
checks.explanation: Patient muscle had fewer satellite cells.

checks.claim: Cells from patients with the homozygous POGLUT1 D233E mutation showed abnormal myogenic differentiation.
checks.evidence_quote: Primary myoblasts from patients showed slow proliferation, facilitated differentiation, and a decreased pool of quiescent PAX7+ cells.
checks.explanation: Patient myoblasts showed abnormal myogenic differentiation.

checks.claim: Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) suggested that impaired Notch signaling and loss of satellite cells contribute to POGLUT1-related LGMD.
checks.evidence_quote: These data suggest that a key pathomechanism for this novel form of muscular dystrophy is Notch-dependent loss of satellite cells.
checks.explanation: The authors propose Notch-dependent loss of satellite cells as a key disease mechanism.

paragraphs.text: Servian-Morilla et al. (2020) found homozygous or compound heterozygous POGLUT1 mutations in further patients with LGMD.

checks.claim: Servian-Morilla et al. (2020) found homozygous or compound heterozygous POGLUT1 mutations in additional patients with LGMD.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing data analysis identified nine missense and one nonsense recessive variants (homozygous or compound heterozygous) in the POGLUT1 gene, in 15 patients from nine independent families
checks.explanation: Homozygous or compound heterozygous variants were found in further LGMD patients.

paragraphs.text: Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) proposed that reduced O-glucosylation of Notch by mutant POGLUT1 lowers Notch signaling. This would deplete the muscle satellite cell pool and impair muscle regeneration. They also observed reduced glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan in patient muscle.

checks.claim: Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) proposed that reduced O-glucosylation of Notch by mutant POGLUT1 lowers Notch signaling.
checks.evidence_quote: these observations suggest that the D233E mutation affects the self‐renewal of SC by reducing Notch signaling, likely due to defective O‐glucosylation
checks.explanation: The authors propose that reduced O-glucosylation lowers Notch signaling.

checks.claim: Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) proposed that reduced Notch signaling due to mutant POGLUT1 depletes the muscle satellite cell pool.
checks.evidence_quote: As a result, the investigated family shows a defect in Notch signaling with a significant depletion of satellite cells, resulting in defective muscle regeneration
checks.explanation: The authors link reduced Notch signaling to depletion of the satellite cell pool.

checks.claim: Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) proposed that reduced Notch signaling due to mutant POGLUT1 impairs muscle regeneration.
checks.evidence_quote: As a result, the investigated family shows a defect in Notch signaling with a significant depletion of satellite cells, resulting in defective muscle regeneration
checks.explanation: The authors link reduced Notch signaling to impaired muscle regeneration.

checks.claim: Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) observed reduced glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan in muscle from patients with POGLUT1 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Western blots showed a reduction in α‐dystroglycan glycosylation in patient muscle
checks.explanation: The authors observed reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation in patient muscle.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Reduced number of satellite cells on muscle biopsy
Muscle MRI showing involvement of inner thigh muscles with sparing of outer parts
Reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation on muscle biopsy

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous family with LGMDR21, Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) found a homozygous asp233-to-glu (D233E) mutation in the POGLUT1 gene. The mutant protein had reduced O-glucosyltransferase activity. Patient muscle showed reduced Notch signaling and fewer satellite cells.

checks.claim: Servian-Morilla et al. (2016) found a homozygous asp233-to-glu (D233E) mutation in the POGLUT1 gene in affected members of a consanguineous family with LGMDR21.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report a homozygous missense mutation (D233E) in the protein O‐glucosyltransferase 1 gene, POGLUT1, in four siblings with autosomal recessive limb‐girdle muscular dystrophy.
checks.explanation: The paper reports homozygous D233E in the affected members of a consanguineous family.

checks.claim: The POGLUT1 D233E mutant protein had reduced O-glucosyltransferase activity.
checks.evidence_quote: The D233E mutation dramatically reduces the O‐glucosyltransferase activity of POGLUT1
checks.explanation: The mutant protein had reduced O-glucosyltransferase activity.

checks.claim: Muscle from patients homozygous for the POGLUT1 D233E mutation showed reduced Notch signaling.
checks.evidence_quote: Decreases in Notch1‐intracellular domain expression and in HES1 mRNA levels in skeletal muscle were detected compared with controls
checks.explanation: Patient muscle showed reduced Notch signaling.

checks.claim: Muscle from patients homozygous for the POGLUT1 D233E mutation showed fewer satellite cells.
checks.evidence_quote: we found a decrease in PAX7 mRNA and fewer PAX7+ cells in the muscle of patients compared with controls
checks.explanation: Patient muscle had fewer satellite cells.
